name: Mike McCarthy

views.text: An offense should be built to make the quarterback successful, and the plan starts with what he already knows.
Protecting the football and controlling the clock matter more than leading the league in yards.
Some identities are not up for debate; a Pittsburgh defense lines up in a 3-4 and plays physical.
A head coach who calls the plays stays in the meeting room and close to the work, which is where he belongs.
When a playoff game gets away, the head coach owns it, and the fix is in the details of how the team prepares.
Following legends is an honor, not a burden; the only answer is another championship.
Contracts and job security are not something to discuss in public; the direction of the team is what he will talk about.

signatures: answers criticism with a calm statement of confidence in the program's direction rather than a rebuttal
lists ball security, time of possession and the run game when asked about the offense
brings up his Greenfield roots and boyhood Steelers fandom when talking about the job

motivation.want: to win one more championship and finish his career as a hometown hero
motivation.fear: that his return is judged a recycled hire rather than a new chapter

want.text: a seventh title for Pittsburgh with Aaron Rodgers

fear.text: that an aging roster gets one last run and misses

voice: Direct and matter-of-fact, with a Pittsburgh plainness that turns openly emotional when he talks about his hometown. He speaks in process terms about preparation, details and the run game, takes responsibility for losses in general language, and refuses to be drawn into contract talk. He praises his quarterback steadily and rarely criticizes a player by name.

evidence.summary: Press conference after Jerry Jones kept him for 2024 following a home playoff loss to Green Bay. He says the program is built to win a title but has not cleared the playoff threshold, takes responsibility for the recent postseason losses, says the team chased big plays, and calls Prescott part of the answer with another level to reach. Tone reported as disappointed but determined. One press conference after a painful loss.

At the combine, after taking play-calling back from Kellen Moore, he expects the offense to change by roughly a third with the same core terminology, says a new voice will challenge Prescott and the offense will be built around him, and says he will trade some production for fewer turnovers. He values the run, balance and a strong defense over leading the league in offense. His stated plan, not results.

Asked about entering the last year of his deal without an extension, he declines to talk about contracts, his own included, and says he is confident in the team's direction and that it will get over the championship hurdle. The writer notes the precedent of Jason Garrett's lame-duck years. Shows how he deflects job-security questions.

Midseason look at his play-calling: Prescott's passing yards per game fell from Moore's era, with more snaps under center, more play action, fewer deep shots and quicker throws. He is described as direct and matter-of-fact, says the team is built on its defense, and points to time of possession and ball security as progress. Prescott stays publicly patient. A snapshot of six games.

Feature on the friendship between Schottenheimer and Dan Quinn. It recounts that McCarthy, who had worked with Schottenheimer before, offered him a consultant role in 2022 when he meant to take a year off, placing him in Quinn's defensive meetings to play the opposing offense. Shows McCarthy's staffing choices and the working link among the three; it is mostly about the other two men.

Introduced as the Steelers' 17th head coach after Mike Tomlin stepped away: visibly emotional, the Greenfield native and boyhood Steelers fan says Pittsburgh is his world, promises a seventh title and jokes the parade will start at his childhood home. Notes fan unease about the hire and a possible Rodgers return. Warm, hometown-focused tone.

At the introduction he says flatly that he will call the offensive plays and run the offense, a first for a Steelers head coach; the 2025 offense with Aaron Rodgers ranked 25th in yards and 15th in scoring. Florio frames it as a big repair job.

Pittsburgh hires Patrick Graham to run McCarthy's defense; McCarthy pledges to keep the 3-4 that has defined the franchise for three decades. Context: the AFC North champion defense fell to 26th in yards, its worst since 1988, with key stars in their 30s. Facts only.
